title: Growth and Patterns of Tourism in World
summary: Growth means the increase or decrease in the number of tourists compared with an earlier period (negative growth if fewer); pattern means the spatial distribution of tourism over the earth. Factors affecting world tourism: high income of the tourist (per capita income is the best guide), paid holidays or holiday entitlement, travel cost (low to moderate cost boosts tourism), technology (information on the internet), package providers and tour operators, media and updated knowledge, a growing middle class in developing countries and the rise of new destinations with more tourism investment.

Cultural (historical and archaeological sites, architecture, monuments, museums, performing arts, cuisine), natural (landscapes, seascapes, mountains, islands, beaches, parks, flora and fauna, caves), events (mega-events, trade fairs, conferences, community events, festivals, religious events such as the Haj and the Maha Kumbh, sports events such as the Olympics, football and cricket world cups), recreational (sightseeing, golf, swimming, tennis, cricket, snow sports, mountaineering, rafting) and entertainment (theme and amusement parks, casinos, shopping, sports complexes). Spatial distribution depends on natural landscape, beautiful sites, accessibility and moderate climate plus man-made beautification; tourism is concentrated in Europe, around the Mediterranean and in the USA, and growing in developing countries.

UNWTO (headquarters at Madrid, Spain) reported that in 2015 France was the top destination (about 67.3 million arrivals as listed in the lesson), then the USA, Spain, Italy, UK, China, Poland, Mexico, Canada and Hungary. World arrivals: 983 million (2011), 1,035 million (2012), 1,087 million (2013), 1,135 million (2014, up 4.3–4.4%) and 1,184 million (2015, up 4.4%), the sixth consecutive year of above-average growth; expected growth about 4% a year. From 530 million in 1995 arrivals nearly doubled to 1,035 million in 2012, crossing a billion for the first time; in 2012 Asia and the Pacific recorded the highest growth (7%). Growth was mainly in East Asia and the Pacific (about 13% a year) and the Middle East (10%). Europe and the Americas held 95% of arrivals in 1950, 82% in 1990 and 76% in 2000.

Share of arrivals in 2015: Europe 609 million (51%), Asia and Pacific 278 million (23%), Americas 191 million, Middle East 54 million and Africa 53 million (5%, the minimum). Tourist arrivals are the persons who arrive at a tourist centre and stay at least a night, counted without any age limit. International tourist receipts are all expenditure by inbound visitors (accommodation, transport, food, entertainment, souvenirs, entry fees). Receipts reached US$ 1,245 billion in 2014 (up 3.7% in real terms), Europe having the largest share (41%), then Asia and the Pacific (30%), the Americas (22%), the Middle East (4%) and Africa (3%). Total exports from international tourism were US$ 1.5 trillion, about US$ 4 billion a day.

Growth outside the developed world became noticeable from 1970. The average world growth is about 4–4.5% a year. By 2020 Europe is projected to have about 717 million tourists (3.1% growth); East Asia and the Pacific to grow 6.5% a year with 25% share (replacing the Americas as second); Africa and the Middle East over 7% and South Asia to reach about 19 million tourists. World Tourism Day is celebrated on 27 September to foster awareness of the importance of tourism.

vsa: 'The trend of international tourist arrivals is almost continuously on the rise.' Support the statement with two relevant arguments.
World arrivals rose from 530 million in 1995 to 1,035 million in 2012 and 1,184 million in 2015. Arrivals grew every year since 2010 by about 4% or more, with only a small dip around 2003.
April 2026
'Package providers are of great help to the tourists.' Analyse the statement in two points.
They prepare the itinerary as per the tourists' demand and make a hassle-free tour. Where tour operators work, tourism is more prominent on the world tourist map.
April 2026
Mention any two attractions for tourists at destinations in the world.
Cultural attractions such as historical sites, monuments and museums. Natural attractions such as landscapes, beaches, mountains and parks, and events such as festivals and sports.
April 2025
Differentiate between natural landscapes and cultural landscapes in two points.

Natural landscapes (mountains, beaches, parks) are created by nature and are attractive for scenery. Cultural landscapes (monuments, museums, architecture, festivals) are created by people and show history and culture.
April 2026
How does travel cost affect tourism in the world?
Moderate to low cost boosts tourism while high cost is a hindrance. It matters less for very rich people.
April 2024
Describe the growth of world tourism since 2011.
Arrivals were 983 million in 2011, 1,087 million in 2013 and 1,184 million in 2015, with growth of about 4% every year.
What is meant by sports tourism?
It is the movement of tourists to take part in or watch sports elsewhere, such as golf, tennis, cricket, snow sports and world cups.
Name any three of the top ten tourist destinations of the world in 2015.
France, the United States and Spain (then Italy, the United Kingdom, China, Poland, Mexico, Canada and Hungary).
Why has the share of Europe and the Americas in world tourism declined?
New destinations in East Asia, the Pacific, the Middle East and other developing regions have grown. These regions grow faster, reducing the share of Europe and America.
sa: Explain any three attractions for the tourists at destinations in the world.

(i) Cultural: historical and archaeological sites, monuments, museums and cuisine. (ii) Natural: landscapes, mountains, beaches, islands, parks, flora and fauna. (iii) Events and recreation: festivals, the Olympics, trade fairs, sightseeing, golf, snow sports and amusement parks.
Explain the factors affecting world tourism in three points (any three).

(i) High income and paid holidays give people money and time to travel. (ii) Low travel cost and technology (internet information) encourage travel. (iii) Package providers, media and the growing middle class of developing countries boost tourism.
Explain the spatial distribution of world tourism in three points.

(i) It depends on natural landscape, beautiful sites, accessibility and moderate climate. (ii) Man-made beautification, monuments, gardens and religious festivals also attract tourists. (iii) It is concentrated in Europe, the Mediterranean and the USA but is growing in developing countries.
Explain the share of the world regions in international tourist arrivals in 2015 (three points).

(i) Europe had the highest share, 609 million (51%). (ii) Asia and the Pacific followed with 278 million (23%), then the Americas with 191 million. (iii) Africa had the minimum, 53 million (5%), and the Middle East 54 million.
Explain the future prospects of world tourism (three points).

(i) Arrivals are expected to grow about 4% a year. (ii) Europe will remain the top destination (about 717 million by 2020) and East Asia and the Pacific will grow 6.5% a year. (iii) Africa, the Middle East and South Asia will grow quickly from a low base.
la: Explain any six factors affecting tourism in the world.

(i) High income and per capita income of tourists. (ii) Paid holidays or holiday entitlement. (iii) Travel cost: low to moderate costs boost tourism. (iv) Technology: information on the internet. (v) Package providers and tour operators make touring easy, and print and audio-visual media create awareness. (vi) A growing middle class in developing countries and new destinations with tourism investment.
Explain the growth and pattern of world tourism in six points.

(i) Tourism flourished from the mid-20th century. (ii) Europe and America had 95% of arrivals in 1950 but 76% by 2000. (iii) East Asia and the Pacific grew about 13% a year and the Middle East 10%. (iv) Arrivals rose from 983 million (2011) to 1,184 million (2015). (v) Europe takes 51% of arrivals and 41% of receipts. (vi) Receipts were US$ 1,245 billion in 2014 and arrivals are expected to grow about 4% a year.
Describe the attractions for tourists at destinations in the world, in six points.

(i) Cultural attractions: historical and archaeological sites, monuments and museums. (ii) Natural attractions: landscapes, seascapes, mountains, beaches, flora and fauna. (iii) Events: mega-events, trade fairs, conferences and community festivals. (iv) Religious events such as the Haj and Maha Kumbh. (v) Sports events such as the Olympics and world cups, and recreation like golf and snow sports. (vi) Entertainment such as theme parks, casinos and shopping.
